title: Online Causal Configuration for Networked Systems via Doubly Robust Steady-State Learning
claim: A closed-loop procedure turns interfering deployments into exposure-adjusted, doubly robust value certificates that drive optimistic configuration selection each round.
layout: 4 numbered panels left-to-right, feedback arrow underneath returning to the start
description: A wide figure of four pastel-tinted panels, numbered 1–4 and joined by grey arrows. Panel 1, 'Black-box deployment setting', stacks a global configuration z box over a network of icons (cell tower, car, cloud, router, building), then adaptive local controllers and post-burn-in telemetry. Panel 2, 'Causal Measurement and Exposure Modeling', shows a network graph mapped to layered exposure planes. Below are two overlapping bell curves, the exploratory law (η>0) and the target deployment law (η=0). Panel 3, 'Doubly Robust Steady-State Evaluation', shows a database of logged data (A, C, R), then outcome and weight model icons combined with a plus sign, ending in a value-estimate curve with uncertainty. Panel 4 shows an upper-bound curve over an estimated-value curve, a select-max step, and the chosen configuration z_t. A bold black arrow underneath, labelled 'Next round: deploy and collect steady-state logs', loops back to panel 1.
caption: The CAUSAL-UCB deployment loop. A global configuration induces interacting local actions; post-burn-in measurements enter an exposure-aware evaluator, whose value certificate guides the next optimistic configuration choice. Visual elements are conceptual.
abstract: Measurement exploration reveals how interacting local controllers behave but can alter the steady-state regime a network operator seeks to optimize. Exploratory rewards may therefore fail to identify a configuration's no-exploration value: under full exploration, identical logged distributions can conceal different target values. Identification requires accounting for both action-law mismatch and shifts in the steady-state context distribution. We introduce CAUSAL-UCB, which selects configurations using optimistic bounds on target causal values. Its interference-aware clipped doubly robust evaluator produces predecision certificates separating statistical variation from calibrated identification, transport, and temporal-dependence errors. For any finite horizon and predetermined schedule of measurement-exploration rates $\{Î·_t\}$, we prove lower bounds of $Î©((1+\sum_tÎ·_t)^{-1/2})$ on minimax inference error and $Î©(\sum_tÎ·_t)$ on measurement-induced deployment loss in a stationary, potentially slow-mixing family. We bound regret under valid certificates and selected-information growth, and establish an anytime finite-sample certificate with a shared radius for estimation, selection, and reporting in a restricted known-local-interference model. In a high-mismatch benchmark with 24 paired seeds and 200 rounds, CAUSAL-UCB attains target regret of $1.732$ versus $6.326$ for certified IPS-UCB, with deployment gaps of $30.607$ and $23.217$, respectively. Independent-audit coverage tests and trace-driven semi-synthetic studies further assess certificate coverage and deployment trade-offs.
